run.question:
Alertmanager alert PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus since 2026-11-17T23:44:53Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The firing alert is the kube-prometheus rule PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers, whose expression in ConfigMap prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-rulefiles-0 (namespace prometheus) is `max_over_time(prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered{job="prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus",namespace="prometheus"}[5m]) < 1` with `for: 10m` and severity warning. Everything that could be enumerated in namespace prometheus at query time belongs to the Prometheus/operator/kube-state-metrics/node-exporter stack: 8 pods, 5 Services, 5 Endpoints subsets, 2 Deployments, 1 StatefulSet and 5 ServiceAccounts, and the cluster-wide StatefulSet list (6 objects) contains no Alertmanager workload either; the Alertmanager CRD (alertmanagers.monitoring.coreos.com) is installed, so no Alertmanager workload is visible anywhere for this Prometheus to discover. The alert's instance 100.96.5.74:9090 is the endpoint of pod prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0, which is Running, Ready and has 0 restarts but was created at 2026-11-17T23:44:21Z, 32 seconds before the alert start, while the rule's 10 m `for` implies the zero-Alertmanager condition began roughly 10 minutes earlier. The driving series prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered is not available in the authorized Prometheus target (63 metric names returned, none prometheus_*), the operator's rule endpoint returned no rules, the configuration lives in unreadable Secrets, Alertmanager custom resources cannot be read in this Run, and the returned events start at 23:52:13Z, after the pod recreation. The alert is therefore best explained by there being no Alertmanager target for this Prometheus, but the object that removed or failed to create it is not verifiable, so the conclusion is partial and no root-cause object is named.

claims.text: The rule PrometheusNotConnectedToAlertmanagers is defined in ConfigMap prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-rulefiles-0 (namespace prometheus), key prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-ac4fa589-688e-4d06-9c48-89982b78688c.yaml, with expr `max_over_time(prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered{job="prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus",namespace="prometheus"}[5m]) < 1`, `for: 10m` and label severity: warning.

The complete pod list of namespace prometheus returned 8 pods and none is an Alertmanager pod: prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator-57d68989cc-hkbnh, prometheus-kube-state-metrics-7c5fb9d798-tqssx, prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 and five prometheus-prometheus-node-exporter-* pods.

Namespace prometheus contains only the StatefulSet prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus (1 replica, 1 ready, created 2026-11-17T00:30:53Z); no Alertmanager StatefulSet exists there, and the cluster-wide StatefulSet list returned 6 StatefulSets (clickhouse, data-recorders x2, kube-system topology-monitor, opensearch, prometheus) with no Alertmanager among them.

Namespace prometheus has 5 Services (prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator, prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus, prometheus-kube-state-metrics, prometheus-operated, prometheus-prometheus-node-exporter) and 5 Endpoints objects with the same names; none is an Alertmanager service or an endpoint on port 9093, and the Prometheus service address for prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 is 100.96.5.74:9090, matching the alert's instance label.

Namespace prometheus contains 2 Deployments only, prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator (image quay.io/prometheus-operator/prometheus-operator:v0.85.0, 1 ready/1 available, created 2026-11-17T00:30:52Z) and prometheus-kube-state-metrics (1 ready/1 available); no Alertmanager Deployment exists there.

Pod prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 is Running with Ready=True conditions and restartCount 0 on both containers (config-reloader, prometheus), and its creationTimestamp is 2026-11-17T23:44:21Z, 32 seconds before the alert start 2026-11-17T23:44:53Z.

The rule files ConfigMap prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-rulefiles-0 has creationTimestamp 2026-11-17T23:37:59Z, later than the stack objects created at 00:30:52-00:30:53Z, and it already carries the otel-demo alerting-rules file alongside the kube-prometheus rule files.

The CRD alertmanagers.monitoring.coreos.com (group monitoring.coreos.com, kind Alertmanager) is installed in the cluster since 2026-11-17T00:30:40Z, so the operator supports Alertmanager objects even though no Alertmanager workload is visible.

The authorized Prometheus target returned 63 metric names in the window 2026-11-17T22:44:53Z-2026-11-18T00:34:31Z (container_*, go_*, traces_span_metrics_*, otelcol_*, process_*, redis_*, jvm_* and a few recording-rule names); none is named prometheus_notifications_* or starts with prometheus_, so the series driving this alert is not observable in that target.

A StatefulSet named prometheus-alert-recorder exists in namespace data-recorders (1 replica, 1 ready) whose container env sets PROMETHEUS_ENDPOINT=http://prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus.prometheus.svc.cluster.local:9090, i.e. a consumer of this Prometheus rather than an Alertmanager.

The alert condition (max_over_time(prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered{...}[5m]) < 1) holds because this Prometheus has no Alertmanager target in its effective configuration and no Alertmanager workload or Service exists in the cluster for it to discover; the enumerated object lists in namespace prometheus and the cluster-wide StatefulSet list contain no Alertmanager pod, service, endpoint or statefulset.

The recreation of pod prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 at 2026-11-17T23:44:21Z and the re-creation of the rule files ConfigMap at 2026-11-17T23:37:59Z suggest a Prometheus stack reconfiguration in that period that could coincide with alertmanager discovery dropping to zero; this remains unproven because the rule's 10 m `for` implies the condition began around 23:34:53Z, and the config secret, the Prometheus custom resource and events for that time are not readable.

Considered and rejected: that the alert is caused by Prometheus itself being down, unready or crash-looping. StatefulSet prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus reports 1 replica and 1 ready, and pod prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 is Running/Ready with restartCount 0 on both containers, so a Prometheus availability failure is not the explanation for the alert.

gaps: The Prometheus configuration is mounted from a Secret (StatefulSet volume 'config'; secret name redacted and Secrets cannot be read), so it is unverified whether alerting.alertmanagers is empty, points at a non-existent service, or was recently removed.

The Alertmanager custom resource (alertmanagers.monitoring.coreos.com) is not a kind this Run could read; the query for it returned nothing usable, so whether an Alertmanager CR exists in namespace prometheus, was deleted in the window, or was never created is unknown, even though its CRD is installed.

The driving series prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered produced no samples for 2026-11-17T22:44:53Z-2026-11-18T00:34:31Z, and the 63 metric names the target returned contain no prometheus_* series, so the alert's actual value (0 versus no data) could not be verified; list_prometheus_rules also returned no rules both with the rule_name filter and without it, so rule/pending state was not confirmed on the target.

The Kubernetes event query filtered on involvedObject.namespace=prometheus returned no matching entries, and the run-level event listing covered only 2026-11-17T23:52:13Z-2026-11-18T00:24:59Z; therefore no event explains the 23:44:21Z pod recreation or the 23:37:59Z ConfigMap recreation, and earlier events may have expired.

fetched logs from pod prometheus-prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus-0 (containers prometheus, config-reloader, init-config-reloader) and from pod prometheus-kube-prometheus-operator-57d68989cc-hkbnh (container kube-prometheus-stack) returned zero lines, and no previous container instance exists, so log evidence for Alertmanager discovery or notification errors is unavailable.

Cluster-wide name/image-filtered checks for 'alertmanager' workloads (pods, services, deployments, statefulsets) returned no matches with status no_data; those empty results are stated limits of what the queries covered and are not used here as proof of absence — absence is asserted only for the fully enumerated namespace-prometheus object lists and the cluster-wide StatefulSet list.

Whether the Alertmanager instance implied by the alert payload (which forwarded the alert to the investigation) exists outside this cluster is unknown; no Alertmanager pod or Service was found inside the cluster.
No baseline of prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered before the incident is available, so how long discovery has been below 1 could not be compared.
next_steps: Read the Prometheus custom resource monitoring.coreos.com/v1 named prometheus-kube-prometheus-prometheus and its generated config secret to confirm whether spec.alerting.alertmanagers is empty or references a Service that does not exist.

Check the kube-prometheus-stack Helm release values (alertmanager.enabled and Alertmanager spec) and whether an Alertmanager named prometheus-kube-prometheus-alertmanager should exist in namespace prometheus; if it was disabled or removed, restoring the Alertmanager StatefulSet/Service and pointing Prometheus spec.alerting.alertmanagers at <alertmanager-service>:9093 is the configuration fix.
After any configuration change, verify prometheus_notifications_alertmanagers_discovered > 0 and that prometheus_notifications_errors_total is not increasing on the Prometheus self-monitoring target.
